<document id=DOC_excerpt_settle_order>
DISCOUNT_BY_TIER = {"standard": 20, "premium": 30}

def settle_order(account_tier, total_amount, coupon_codes, coupon_lookup):
    discount = DISCOUNT_BY_TIER[account_tier]
    coupon_sum = coupon_lookup[coupon_codes[0]]
    amount_owed = total_amount * discount / 100 - coupon_sum
    return amount_owed
</document>

The module above redeems coupon codes by looking them up. Nothing in
it limits how long a code stays redeemable, so every code ever issued
remains valid indefinitely.

Recommend how the design should bound a code's lifetime, and say what
the lookup would have to carry for that bound to be enforceable.

response.text:
Give every code an explicit validity window and refuse redemption outside it. A code that never records when it stops being redeemable cannot be expired by the lookup.

The lookup must carry, per code, the redeemable value plus the bound itself—at least an `expires_at` instant (or `valid_from` and `valid_until`). A relative TTL only works if the record also carries the anchor time it is measured from (for example `issued_at`). At settlement, resolve the code, compare the redemption time to that bound, and apply the value only if the code is still inside the window. A bare `code → amount` map, which is all this function uses, has nothing to enforce.
